body.reads: The rule checks tcp_goodput_bps in sched_cubic against 0, with the planned scheduler simulation compared against the already measured default zero in E0.
body.follows_why: G2 says per-flow scheduling would give TCP a link share, so a positive tcp_goodput_bps is the measure and direction it requires, and the threshold >0 is weaker than a link share rather than clearly outside it.
body.honest_why: tcp_goodput_bps@sched_cubic is not in E0, T2, T3, or T4, and a scheduler that still leaves TCP at 0 would fail the rule.
body.consistent_why: The planned simulation changes only the sender-side queue to a scheduler while keeping l1.queue.length=100 and TcpCubic, and the competing guess Y3 is also about the same zero tcp_goodput_bps seen in E0.
body.correct_why: If G2 is true, scheduler service should give TCP a link share and make tcp_goodput_bps positive; if Y3 is true and G2 false, Cubic's loss response still prevents payload delivery and tcp_goodput_bps remains 0.

body.reads: The rule checks tcp_goodput_bps in bbr_fifo against 0, with the planned TcpBbr simulation compared against the already measured default zero in E0.
body.follows_why: G1 says TcpCubic's loss response prevents payload delivery, so changing only tcp.type to TcpBbr should make tcp_goodput_bps positive, and the threshold >0 is not clearly outside what that guess could give.
body.honest_why: tcp_goodput_bps@bbr_fifo is not in E0, T2, T3, or T4, and TcpBbr under the same FIFO queue could still measure 0.
body.consistent_why: The planned simulation changes only tcp.type from TcpCubic to TcpBbr with l1.queue.length=100, and the competing guess Y4 is about the same zero tcp_goodput_bps result in E0 and T2.
body.correct_why: If G1 is true, a different loss response should avoid the Cubic collapse and deliver TCP bytes; if Y4 is true and G1 false, FIFO starvation should still leave tcp_goodput_bps at 0.

body.reads: The rule checks tcp_goodput_bps in queue1000_fifo against 0, with the planned 1000-packet queue simulation compared against the already measured default zero in E0.
body.follows_why: G3 says a 1000-packet queue would admit handshake packets and allow some TCP delivery, so positive tcp_goodput_bps is the measure and direction it requires, and >0 is not clearly outside that claim.
body.honest_why: tcp_goodput_bps@queue1000_fifo is not in E0, T2, T3, or T4, and a 1000-packet FIFO queue could still measure 0.
body.consistent_why: The planned simulation changes only l1.queue.length from 100 to 1000 under TcpCubic, and the competing guess Y4 is about the same zero tcp_goodput_bps result in E0 and T2.
body.correct_why: If G3 is true, queue1000_fifo should show positive tcp_goodput_bps, but if Y4 is true it only says FIFO scheduling starves TCP and per-flow scheduling is needed for a link share, so a larger FIFO queue might still allow some handshake delivery and positive goodput.
body.feedback: Correct does not pass: against Y4, the rule rests on E0 tcp_goodput_bps=0 and T2 l1_q=99 or 100, but Y4 does not clearly predict that a 1000-packet FIFO queue must still have zero goodput, only that FIFO scheduling prevents a link share. A repaired test must make the competing cause predict no TCP delivery at all under the larger queue, or test a consequence that separates larger-queue admission from FIFO scheduling starvation.

body.reads: The rule compares the measured tcp_goodput_bps in the new queue1000_fifo and queue1000_scheduler runs, requiring both to be greater than zero.
body.follows_why: H3 follows from Y5 because Y5 says a 1000-packet FIFO queue can admit TCP handshake packets and allow some TCP delivery, so a positive tcp_goodput_bps is the required direction and the threshold >0 is not outside what Y5 could give.
body.honest_why: The rule can fail because both compared tcp_goodput_bps values are from new runs not already in E0 or T1-T9, and a zero in either new run would fail the >0 checks.
body.consistent_why: H3 claims only that increasing l1.queue.length to 1000 under TcpCubic makes tcp_goodput_bps positive, but the rule also requires a second positive result from a structurally different run, so it tests more than H3 and the compared runs differ by structure rather than only the claimed queue-length change.
body.correct_why: If Y5 is true and Y4 false, Y5 implies only the larger-FIFO positive result, not the extra structurally different positive result, so the rule's outcome cannot be told; if Y4 is true and Y5 false, Y4 predicts FIFO starvation so the FIFO positive check fails.
body.feedback: Consistent and Correct do not pass: the rule adds a second required positive result that H3 does not claim and Y5 does not imply, so it can fail even when the larger-queue admission guess is true; E0 tcp_goodput_bps=0 and T2 l1_q=99 or 100 show starvation at queue 100 but do not by themselves make Y4 predict zero TCP delivery at queue 1000. A repaired test must make the competing FIFO-starvation cause predict no TCP delivery under the larger queue, or test a consequence that separates larger-queue admission from FIFO scheduling starvation, without requiring an outcome not implied by the tested guess.

body.because: C5 failed because r010 measured tcp_goodput_bps=463881280, only about 1.3% below r002's 482007923 and above the 95% threshold 457907527, so the queue-4 goodput did not fall as the tested guess predicted.
body.shows: The measured sched_q4 run r010 has tcp_goodput_bps=463881280, which is above the threshold 457907527, so check C5 failed.

honest.why: Before r010 ran, its tcp_goodput_bps was not in the records, and the 95% threshold 457907527 is not one that almost any result passes, so the test could have failed.

consistent.why: The rule checks exactly the hypothesis's claim about scheduler TcpCubic at l1.queue.length=4 using r010's tcp_goodput_bps, and the competing guess Y16 is about the same scheduler TcpCubic result r002.

correct.why: If the tested guess were true, r010's tcp_goodput_bps would be below 457907527 and C5 would hold, whereas if Y16's scheduler-share explanation were true, TcpCubic would remain near the scheduler share and C5 would fail as measured.

body.text: Under scheduler TcpCubic, r010 with l1.queue.length=4 has tcp_retrans=3417 and l1_drops_tcp=3416 while r009 with l1.queue.length=1000 has tcp_retrans=0 and l1_drops_tcp=0, and no shown record explains this queue-length-dependent TCP loss pattern.
body.name: Scheduler TCP loss pattern

body.observations: F7 and F8 ask why scheduler TcpCubic with l1.queue.length=4 has tcp_retrans=3417 and l1_drops_tcp=3416, while l1.queue.length=1000 has tcp_retrans=0 and l1_drops_tcp=0.
